Compare two tables value by value

Source: R/diff-table.R
diff_table.Rd

x is the benchmark: in the default mode = "benchmark" it is the source of truth, and y is the table being tested against it. With mode = "equal" the two are peers, and the question is simply whether they are equal. Rows are aligned on their identity columns and every numeric measure is compared, one row per value, each traceable to its source row in both tables.

Usage

diff_table(
  x,
  y,
  mode = c("benchmark", "equal"),
  by = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  row_key = c("none", "position", "sorted"),
  measures = "numeric",
  tolerance = 0,
  rel_tol = 0,
  duplicates = c("disambiguate", "aggregate", "error"),
  cast = mode == "benchmark",
  truncate = TRUE,
  nan_is_na = TRUE,
  date_format = "%Y-%m-%d"
)

Arguments

x

The benchmark table (in "equal" mode, simply the first table).

y

The table to compare with it.

mode

"benchmark" (the default) or "equal". See Modes.

by

Identity columns, by name, in either spelling. NULL (the default) uses every column that is not a measure.

exclude

Columns to leave out of the comparison, by name, in either spelling. They are removed from both tables before anything else, in either mode: an excluded column need not be in both tables, is not announced as dropped or ignored, and does not stop mode = "equal" from calling the rest equal. A name in neither table is a warning, not an error, so one list of technical columns can serve many tables; a name that by or measures also names is an error.

row_key

"none" (the default), "position" or "sorted": add a virtual row_number key column. See Well-formed tables.

measures

"numeric" (the default) compares the double columns; "numeric+integer" the integer columns too. Or column names, which must be numeric or integer, or character(0) for none, which compares whole rows.

tolerance

The largest absolute difference still counted as same.

rel_tol

The largest relative difference still counted as same, relative to the larger magnitude of the two values. A value is same when it is within either tolerance.

duplicates

"disambiguate" (the default), "aggregate" or "error". See Duplicate keys.

cast

Whether to cast y to x's types. Defaults to TRUE in benchmark mode; with FALSE the types must already agree. Equal mode never casts.

truncate

Whether a cast may drop a fraction. See Truncation.

nan_is_na

Whether NaN and NA are the same missing value.

date_format

The format text dates are read in when cast to Date. Text must match it exactly, so a string that merely starts with a date is refused rather than read as one.

Value

A data.table keyed by the identity columns (and key_seq, metric when present), with status a factor with levels same, changed, only_x and only_y. The key includes row_number when row_key added it. Its shape is in attr(d, "shape"):

  • "cells", the usual one: one row per row and measure, with key_seq (only when duplicates were numbered), metric, row_id_x, row_id_y (the source rows, NA on the side the row is missing from), value_x, value_y, diff (value_y - value_x), abs_diff (abs(diff)), rel_diff (abs_diff / pmax(abs(value_x), abs(value_y)), 0 when both are 0, NA unless both are finite) and status.

  • "groups", with duplicates = "aggregate": one row per key and measure, with n_rows_x, n_rows_y, n_na_x, n_na_y, value_key_x, value_key_y (the exact multiset of values, as hexadecimal text from the C library: compare them within one session, not with text stored on another platform) and status. Without measures only the row counts are compared.

  • "rows", when there are no measures: one row per row, with key_seq (when present), row_id_x, row_id_y and status, which is never changed.

The attributes mode, tolerance (abs and rel), name_map (each column's name in x and y), dropped (columns of y dropped in benchmark mode), excluded (the columns exclude removed, as named in x or y), ignored (columns not compared) and truncated (the casts that truncated, with the rows of y each one touched) record what was done on the way.

Modes

  • "benchmark": does y match the benchmark x? Columns of y that x does not have are dropped, with a message. A column of x missing from y is an error. Each compared column of y (in by or measures) is cast to the type it has in x (see cast_rules()), so a number stored as text, or a double stored as an integer, still compares. Columns that are not compared are neither cast nor type-checked. A number cast to text is written with the decimals x uses, when every value of x's column uses the same number of them: 2 in y becomes "2.0" to meet x's "2.0", which a message announces. A value of x that equals one of y's as a number but not as text is warned about, since those rows will not align.

  • "equal": are x and y equal? Every column must be in both tables and have the same type in both; nothing is cast. The result is symmetric: swapping x and y swaps only_x with only_y and negates diff.

Column names

Column names are normalized in both tables before anything else: upper case, with every run of characters other than letters and digits replaced by _, and _ trimmed from the ends. Letters outside ASCII are kept, so Größe and Grüße stay two columns. So unit price, Unit.Price and UNIT_PRICE are one column, in either table. Two names in one table that normalize to the same thing are an error to fix before comparing. The result uses the normalized names; attr(d, "name_map") maps them back.

Truncation

In benchmark mode a cast that drops a fraction – a double to an integer, a number or a timestamp to a whole day – is made by default, because the benchmark's types are taken as the truth: storage such as Spark or Delta turns a locally built double into an integer, and the comparison has to follow it. Each truncation is announced in a message and recorded in attr(d, "truncated"): per column, the count, up to three examples, and in the list column rows the row numbers of y that were truncated, which are the row_id_y of the result. A truncated key column can pair rows that differ (1.5 in y becomes 1 and aligns with x's 1), so read the message when it names a key, and find the rows with d[row_id_y %in% attr(d, "truncated")$rows[[1]]]. Set truncate = FALSE to refuse such casts instead.

Measures and identity

The measures are the numeric columns compared value by value; measures picks them by type or by name, always from x. The row identity is by when given, otherwise every column that is not a measure. With by given, a column in neither role is not compared: that is announced in benchmark mode and an error in equal mode, which cannot call two tables equal while ignoring a column. A numeric column that is part of the identity is matched exactly, with no tolerance. So is a Date key, on its exact value: a Date can hold a fraction of a day, and two Dates that print as the same day then do not align.

With no measures at all the question becomes do the two tables have the same rows?, and the result has one row per row (see Value).

Well-formed tables

A table must have at least one key column to be compared; it may have no measures. When every column is a measure there is nothing to align rows on, and diff_table() refuses unless it is given a key: by, fewer measures, or a virtual one with row_key, which adds a row_number key column to both tables:

  • "position" numbers the rows as they come, so row i of x pairs with row i of y, and a different row order shows as differences.

  • "sorted" numbers the rows after sorting both tables by all their compared columns, so row order does not matter. Compared exactly, that pairs the tables as multisets of rows, and cannot pass two tables that hold different rows. It can pair badly instead: one changed value can move its row within the sort, and the rows after it then pair with the wrong partners and show as changes too. With other key columns, rows are sorted and numbered within each of their groups.

Duplicate keys

When the identity does not tell rows apart, duplicates decides:

  • "disambiguate" numbers the rows of each repeated key in arrival order (key_seq) and pairs them by that number, with a warning: the pairing is an assumption. Reordered rows then show as changes, never as matches. Without measures the repeated rows are identical in every compared column, so pairing them assumes nothing and there is no warning.

  • "aggregate" compares the multiset of values of each key and measure instead, exactly (tolerance must be 0).

  • "error" refuses.

Values

A value is same when both are equal, or when both are finite and their difference is within tolerance or within rel_tol relative to the larger of the two: abs_diff <= tolerance or rel_diff <= rel_tol. Both tolerances default to 0, so by default only equal values are the same. Two missing values are the same; with nan_is_na = TRUE NaN and NA are the same missing value, in measures and in key columns alike.

Conditions

Every condition diff_table() signals has a class, so it can be caught or tested for without matching its text, and inherits from dazdiff_error, dazdiff_warning or dazdiff_message. An error means the question cannot be answered; a warning, that the answer may be wrong; a message reports an expected consequence of the settings.

  • dazdiff_error_input: an argument is malformed.

  • dazdiff_error_columns: columns missing, unknown, or not compared in equal mode; names that are empty or collide once normalized.

  • dazdiff_error_types: a column of a type that cannot be compared, or types that differ where nothing is cast.

  • dazdiff_error_cast: a value that cannot be cast to the benchmark's type.

  • dazdiff_error_keys: no key column to align rows on.

  • dazdiff_error_measures: measures names something that cannot be measured, or a column by names too.

  • dazdiff_error_duplicates: repeated keys under duplicates = "error".

  • dazdiff_error_disjoint: no key appears in both tables. Its field disjoint_columns names the key columns that alone share no value, and constant_columns those among them holding one value in each table (a run id, a source tag), which usually belong in exclude.

  • dazdiff_error_dependency: a suggested package is needed but missing.

  • dazdiff_warning_duplicates: repeated keys paired in arrival order.

  • dazdiff_warning_exclude: exclude names a column in neither table.

  • dazdiff_warning_cast_format: a number of y cast to text does not match x's text for the same number ("2.00" against "2").

  • dazdiff_message_dropped_columns, dazdiff_message_ignored_columns, dazdiff_message_no_measures, dazdiff_message_truncation, dazdiff_message_cast_format: columns of y dropped, columns not compared, no measures, values truncated, numbers written as text in x's format.

Examples

benchmark <- data.frame(id = 1:4, amount = c(10, 20, 30, 40))
tested <- data.frame(
  ID = c("1", "2", "3", "5"),
  Amount = c(10, 20.5, 30, 50),
  loaded_at = "2024-01-01"
)
d <- diff_table(benchmark, tested)
#> Dropped column(s) of `y` that the benchmark `x` does not have: loaded_at.
d
#> Key: <ID, metric>
#>       ID metric row_id_x row_id_y value_x value_y  diff abs_diff   rel_diff
#>    <int> <char>    <int>    <int>   <num>   <num> <num>    <num>      <num>
#> 1:     1 AMOUNT        1        1      10    10.0   0.0      0.0 0.00000000
#> 2:     2 AMOUNT        2        2      20    20.5   0.5      0.5 0.02439024
#> 3:     3 AMOUNT        3        3      30    30.0   0.0      0.0 0.00000000
#> 4:     4 AMOUNT        4       NA      40      NA    NA       NA         NA
#> 5:     5 AMOUNT       NA        4      NA    50.0    NA       NA         NA
#>     status
#>     <fctr>
#> 1:    same
#> 2: changed
#> 3:    same
#> 4:  only_x
#> 5:  only_y
d[status != "same"]
#> Key: <ID, metric>
#>       ID metric row_id_x row_id_y value_x value_y  diff abs_diff   rel_diff
#>    <int> <char>    <int>    <int>   <num>   <num> <num>    <num>      <num>
#> 1:     2 AMOUNT        2        2      20    20.5   0.5      0.5 0.02439024
#> 2:     4 AMOUNT        4       NA      40      NA    NA       NA         NA
#> 3:     5 AMOUNT       NA        4      NA    50.0    NA       NA         NA
#>     status
#>     <fctr>
#> 1: changed
#> 2:  only_x
#> 3:  only_y

# Equal mode: no casting, every column in both tables.
diff_table(benchmark, benchmark, mode = "equal")
#> Key: <ID, metric>
#>       ID metric row_id_x row_id_y value_x value_y  diff abs_diff rel_diff
#>    <int> <char>    <int>    <int>   <num>   <num> <num>    <num>    <num>
#> 1:     1 AMOUNT        1        1      10      10     0        0        0
#> 2:     2 AMOUNT        2        2      20      20     0        0        0
#> 3:     3 AMOUNT        3        3      30      30     0        0        0
#> 4:     4 AMOUNT        4        4      40      40     0        0        0
#>    status
#>    <fctr>
#> 1:   same
#> 2:   same
#> 3:   same
#> 4:   same

# Leave a column out of the comparison, in either table.
diff_table(benchmark, tested, exclude = "loaded_at")
#> Key: <ID, metric>
#>       ID metric row_id_x row_id_y value_x value_y  diff abs_diff   rel_diff
#>    <int> <char>    <int>    <int>   <num>   <num> <num>    <num>      <num>
#> 1:     1 AMOUNT        1        1      10    10.0   0.0      0.0 0.00000000
#> 2:     2 AMOUNT        2        2      20    20.5   0.5      0.5 0.02439024
#> 3:     3 AMOUNT        3        3      30    30.0   0.0      0.0 0.00000000
#> 4:     4 AMOUNT        4       NA      40      NA    NA       NA         NA
#> 5:     5 AMOUNT       NA        4      NA    50.0    NA       NA         NA
#>     status
#>     <fctr>
#> 1:    same
#> 2: changed
#> 3:    same
#> 4:  only_x
#> 5:  only_y

# No key at all: align rows by sorting both tables by their values.
diff_table(
  data.frame(a = c(3, 1, 2), b = c(30, 10, 20)),
  data.frame(a = c(1, 2, 3), b = c(10, 25, 30)),
  row_key = "sorted"
)
#> Key: <row_number, metric>
#>    row_number metric row_id_x row_id_y value_x value_y  diff abs_diff rel_diff
#>         <int> <char>    <int>    <int>   <num>   <num> <num>    <num>    <num>
#> 1:          1      A        2        1       1       1     0        0      0.0
#> 2:          1      B        2        1      10      10     0        0      0.0
#> 3:          2      A        3        2       2       2     0        0      0.0
#> 4:          2      B        3        2      20      25     5        5      0.2
#> 5:          3      A        1        3       3       3     0        0      0.0
#> 6:          3      B        1        3      30      30     0        0      0.0
#>     status
#>     <fctr>
#> 1:    same
#> 2:    same
#> 3:    same
#> 4: changed
#> 5:    same
#> 6:    same

# No measures: do the tables have the same rows?
diff_table(data.frame(k = c("a", "b")), data.frame(k = c("b", "c", "a")))
#> No measure columns (measures = "numeric"), so rows are compared as wholes: do the two tables have the same rows?
#> Key: <K>
#>         K row_id_x row_id_y status
#>    <char>    <int>    <int> <fctr>
#> 1:      a        1        3   same
#> 2:      b        2        1   same
#> 3:      c       NA        2 only_y
